data.name: Harveer
data.gender_notes: Harveer is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Harveer is derived from the name Hari, which is a popular name for the Hindu deity Vishnu, known as the preserver of the universe. Harveer means 'God of Gods' or 'Lord Hari'. The name holds immense spiritual significance and is believed to bring prosperity, happiness, and good fortune to the bearer. The name Harveer carries the meaning “God of Gods, Lord Hari” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Harveer usually hope their child will grow to embody god of gods, lord hari and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Harveer belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Gods, Lord Hari.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harveer total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Harveer as a name has its roots deeply established in Hindu culture. The name is derived from Hari, which is a well-known name for Lord Vishnu. Vishnu, as one of the primary deities in Hinduism, is revered for preserving the universe and maintaining the cosmic order. Harveer's association with this deity adds to the cultural significance of the name. Moreover, the name is popular amongst Hindu communities and is often given as a birth name.
data.spiritual_significance: Harveer holds immense spiritual significance in Hindu culture. As the name refers to Lord Hari, it is believed to connect the bearer with divinity. Lord Hari is associated with compassion, love, and preservation, and is believed to bring happiness, prosperity, and good fortune to the individual named Harveer. Furthermore, the name resonates with the spiritual values of Hinduism, instilling a deep sense of reverence, devotion, and faith in the bearer.
